title: AI UGC Video Ads for TikTok and Reels | AIVideosUGC
description: Create AI UGC video ads with a casual creator-style look from a product photo. Download the clip and add captions in TikTok, Reels, or Facebook.
h1: AI UGC Video Ads With a Casual, Creator-Style Look
lead: Make short UGC-style video ads for TikTok, Reels and Shorts from one product photo. The person in the video is AI-generated, so show the product, not a fake review.

steps.d: Well lit, with the whole product in frame.
Name the setting and one action, such as filling a reusable bottle at the kitchen sink. Pick 9:16 for TikTok and Reels.
Type the headline and offer in CapCut or Ads Manager.

faq.q: What should I write in the description?
faq.a: One everyday moment with your product in it. Name the place, the light, and the action, for example “sunny bathroom counter, hand picks up the soap bar and turns it.” Keep it to a single scene so the clip stays focused.

faq.q: Can I present an AI-generated person as a real customer?
faq.a: No. The person and scene are AI-generated; they are not customer footage or a real endorsement.

faq.q: Can I add captions, a price, or music?
faq.a: Yes, once the clip is downloaded. Captions and music go on in TikTok or CapCut, and prices or discount codes can be added in CapCut or Ads Manager. Typing text yourself avoids the spelling slips that AI-made lettering can have.

faq.q: Can I make a product demonstration ad?
faq.a: Yes. Start with a clear product reference and describe one believable action a customer can understand.

faq.q: Can I choose a square or vertical output?
faq.a: Yes. The available video size choices include 9:16, 1:1, 16:9 and other configured ratios.

faq.q: How many credits does a video ad cost?
faq.a: A 6-second clip costs 24 credits, a 10-second clip 40 credits and a 15-second clip 60 credits. The editor shows the cost before you generate.

overview.h2: Keep the product at the center of a casual scene
overview.p: A casual scene can show a product in an ordinary moment, such as packing a lunch bag or picking up a speaker. The person and setting are AI-generated.

examples.lead: See how creators can demonstrate products with a try-on, an unboxing, a routine or a clear before-and-after.

steps.sourceAlt: Your product: green glass bottle beside a water glass at a bright kitchen sink.
steps.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as the product and keep its shape, color and label area exactly. At a bright kitchen counter, an adult hand lifts the green glass bottle once and holds it still toward the camera. Clean daylight, natural kitchen-ad look. Close side angle with one slow push-in as the bottle rises. End with the bottle held steady above the counter. Sound: a soft bottle-set-down tone and quiet kitchen ambience; no music.

cards.label: Car Selfie Review: Vitamin C Serum
cards.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as the product and keep its shape, color and label area exactly. An adult woman sits in a parked car in daylight, holds the serum beside her face and says: “One pump, then a light pass over the cheek.” She applies one pump and ends looking into the lens with the bottle visible. Natural skin texture, casual creator-ad look. Chest-up front-facing handheld framing with slight sway. End with the bottle front beside her cheek after the single pump. Sound: her voice, one pump click and light street ambience; no music.

Soft morning window light, natural skin texture, casual GRWM ad look. Chest-up mirror framing with one gentle push-in. End facing the mirror with the lip balm tube beside her lips. cards.label: Street Interview: Protein Bar First Bite

Natural morning light, direct creator-demo look. Chest-up eye-level handheld framing with slight sway. Sound: spoken line, zipper pull and birds; no music.
